title: The AI selloff reveals a financing divide: revenue today versus returns tomorrow

summary.changed: Friday's broad selloff took the S&P into correction and Nasdaq down 10% on the week.
summary.missed: Stock-price losses do not prove canceled chip demand; financing risk and future returns differ from current supplier revenue.
summary.watch: Monday breadth, yields, Nvidia disclosures, hyperscaler capex and free cash flow.

sections.heading: The connecting story: markets are repricing financing quality, not just AI growth
paragraphs: Friday, November 20 brought a severe selloff: Nasdaq lost 5.28% and the S&P 500 fell 3.70%. At 07:45 Israel time on Monday, November 23, regular US trading had not yet opened. The figures below are Friday closes, not live quotes.

The thesis: the distinction between chip vendors already booking revenue and infrastructure buyers financing capex and seeking returns over years has become critical. Falling stock prices alone do not prove collapsing end demand.

sections.heading: Indexes: the selloff is sharp and broad
paragraphs: According to AP, November 20 closes were S&P 500 6,910.39 (−3.70%), Nasdaq 22,617.73 (−5.28%), Dow 48,147.33 (−1.93%) and Russell 2000 2,581.79 (−2.76%). Weekly changes were −8.6%, −10.0%, −8.0% and −7.5%, respectively.

Year to date, AP reports S&P +0.9%, Nasdaq −2.7%, Dow +0.2%, Russell +4.0%. The S&P is more than 10% below its October high, a correction by the usual definition. Russell's relative YTD resilience indicates dispersion but does not establish net fund inflows.

sections.heading: Semiconductors and governance: Nvidia headlines do not establish wrongdoing
paragraphs: Reuters reported Nvidia down roughly 14% Friday and said reports of SEC accounting scrutiny contributed to concerns. A reported investigation is not a finding of a legal violation; without an official conclusion, its outcome cannot be asserted.

Sharp declines among other chip suppliers may reflect sector-wide risk reduction. Actual order cancellations, revised profit estimates, financing costs and multiple compression are distinct mechanisms.

sections.heading: Treasuries and rates: safe-haven demand versus restrictive policy expectations
paragraphs: Reuters reported the US 10-year yield falling around 12 basis points to roughly 4.93% Friday amid safe-haven demand. This is a rounded reported figure, not a separately retrieved official Treasury observation.

Lower long yields generally support long-duration bond prices, including TLT, but no verified TLT closing quote is available here. Lower discount rates can support equity valuations without offsetting weaker future earnings.

sections.heading: Sectors, funds and capital flows: what the evidence can and cannot show
paragraphs: Reuters described broad reductions in AI and technology exposure, alongside some relative investor interest in cloud, cybersecurity and nontechnology businesses. These are market participants' views, not verified ETF flow measurements.

Establishing a transfer of capital from chips into bonds would require verified ETF creations/redemptions and careful separation of primary and secondary trading. Those data were not verified today, so no flow totals are asserted.

sections.heading: Commodities and FX: do not fill missing prices
paragraphs: The equity rout coincided with reports of weakness in gold and bitcoin, but comparable official closing figures for oil, copper, gold, USD/ILS and DXY across the period were not verified here. No numerical daily or annual changes are presented for them.
Economically, cheaper oil can ease some inflation pressure, while a stronger dollar can weigh on overseas revenues of US companies. Directional reasoning is not a substitute for verified quotes.

sections.heading: What markets may be missing: cash-flow test, not headline test
paragraphs: Equipment suppliers can report strong sales while their customers are still building infrastructure whose eventual return is unproven. For MU, WDC and electrical-equipment suppliers, watch backlog conversion, pricing, margins, inventory and free cash flow after capex.
Valuation requires EPS scenarios, DCF and comparable multiples under different rate assumptions. A lower share price alone does not prove that intrinsic value has risen.

sections.heading: Catalysts for the week and the contrarian case
paragraphs: At Monday's November 23 open, monitor market breadth, Treasury yields, VIX, official Nvidia disclosures and revisions to hyperscaler capex plans. No unverified numerical macro forecasts are presented.

Bear case: expensive financing and deferred projects compress both orders and multiples. Bull case: crowded positions are being unwound, underlying demand holds and cash generation validates expectations. The decisive test is ROIC versus WACC, not the size of a one-day decline.
